What happens, in order, and why
1 The customer calls the sales person to get a price they can trust.
2 The sales person lists the items and the difficulty in the quote, and prices them from the price list so the price is fair.
3 The sales person checks availability for a likely date, then asks the manager to confirm it, because availability can lag.
4 The manager holds the date in the day plan and confirms it, so nobody is promised twice.
5 The sales person confirms with the customer one last time; the customer's yes locks the price in the quote.
6 The customer pays the deposit through the payment provider, and it is recorded in the customer account.
7 The manager names the crew and the trucks in the day plan, schedules their work and gives the foreman and movers instructions.
8 On the day the crew sets off. From then on the foreman, not the sales person, is in touch with the customer.
9 The foreman records the arrival and prices any extras from the price list.
10 The foreman records the move as done. The balance falls due: the price plus extras, minus the deposit.
11 The customer pays the balance; the owner's books record it and pay the sales person a share.
• The manager's hold usually lasts the day. It ends if
the customer can't be reached or cancels.
• Cancelling within 7 days of the move: the company
• The company can't do the move: the deposit is returned.
• The customer can't dispute the foreman's extras; the
• Only the manager writes the day plan, so nobody is
on two moves the same day.
• A rebooked move is the same move with a new date:
a new hold, a new crew, a new day in Moves.
• A move that didn't happen is recorded by the manager
in the day plan, with the reason and whose fault it was.
